Saffron Catter N Cakes

Served at: St. Catherine's Day

Makes 12 bunsPrep 30 min (plus 2-3 hours rising time)Cook 20-25 min

Saffron Catter N Cakes, also known as St. Catherine's Buns, are a traditional sweet, yeasted bread baked in England to celebrate St. Catherine's Day on November 25th. Historically, these rich, saffron-infused buns were made by young unmarried women, known as "Catherinettes," who would share them with friends and neighbors as a symbol of good luck and community. Their vibrant golden hue from the saffron is a distinctive and festive characteristic.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 teaspoon saffron threads
  • 1 cup (240 ml) warm milk (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, divided
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast
  • 4 cups (480 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 cup (56 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
  • 1 large egg, lightly beaten
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) currants or raisins (optional)
  • For Glaze: 1 tablespoon milk
  • For Glaze: 1 tablespoon granulated sugar

Method

  1. Crumble saffron threads into the warm milk and let steep for at least 10 minutes to infuse color and flavor.
  2. In a large bowl, combine the saffron-infused milk with 1 tablespoon of the granulated sugar and sprinkle the active dry yeast over the top. Let stand for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  3. In a separate large bowl, whisk together the flour, remaining granulated sugar, and salt.
  4. Pour the yeast mixture, melted butter, and beaten egg into the dry ingredients. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
  5. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, or until smooth and elastic. If using, knead in the currants or raisins during the last minute.
  6. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  7. Gently punch down the dough and divide it into 12 equal pieces. Shape each piece into a round bun.
  8. Place the buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them. Cover loosely and let rise again for 45-60 minutes, or until noticeably puffy.
  9. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
  10. In a small bowl, whisk together the 1 tablespoon milk and 1 tablespoon sugar for the glaze. Brush the tops of the risen buns with this mixture.
  11. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
  12. Transfer the buns to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving warm.

Tips

  • For a deeper saffron flavor, steep the saffron in warm milk for an hour or even overnight in the refrigerator.
  • If you prefer a richer bun, you can add an extra egg yolk to the dough.
  • These buns are best enjoyed fresh on St. Catherine's Day, but leftovers can be stored in an airtight container for a day or two and gently reheated.
